output.brief: What is going on: the remote promotion gap is mostly explained by time in level, not by where people work. Under the policy, staff need 18 months in level to be nominated. Only 32% of remote staff meet that, against 74% of office staff. Among eligible staff, remote and office promotion rates are nearly the same (20.0% vs 21.1%), and nomination rates are similar (28.2% vs 28.6%). The remaining 1-point difference could be chance. Proximity bias is not supported as the main driver, and the COO's three-day office rule (A1) would penalise remote staff on a diagnosis the data does not support. I am fairly sure of this, but I did not check stretch assignments, attrition, or whether remote staff were concentrated in fewer-promotion job families. Next steps: put the attendance rule on hold. Report promotion rates for eligible staff only, by arrangement. Re-check at the FY2027 cycle. Separately, look at remote hiring and the time-in-level pipeline, and at whether remote staff get fewer stretch assignments.
